::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** February 21st [1880s?]  
**Manuscript:** MS Miss Barbara Dennis/7
:::

My dear [Mary](people/person_1628.qmd)[^1]

In the autumn a Mr Yonge in America, an Engineer chose to send me the photograph of his little daughter whom he had named Charlotte and he sent a description of his arms, wanting to know whether he could be of the same family.[^2]  They were not the same as ours, nor as those to which we failed to shew our claim but [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) thought they were the same as yours.  Now, American as he is, he has written the long letter which I send in case your husband can gratify him with an answer tracing his Philip and Mary.  I am sure he would instantly claim you, if he knew that you had a Philip.

I hope you are quite well.  The measles have started in the parish here most inopportunely just before the Government Inspection  We rather expect that [Joanna](people/person_388.qmd) will have them, as her great playfellow is in the midst

your affectionate cousin
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Mary Isabel (Yonge) Yonge (1849-1915), was the second daughter of CMY’s first cousin the Rev. John Eyre Yonge.  She married (1872) the Rev. Denys Nelson Yonge (no relation), Vicar of Boreham, Chelmsford.  Her second son was Philip Caynton Yonge (1877-1928).
[^2]: CMY's American correspondent may have been [Samuel H. Yonge](people/person_2391.qmd).
